page: Microsoft Azure M128dms_v2 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine provisioned on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance features 128 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel processor alongside 3892.0 GB of system memory. This configuration provides a high memory allocation ratio of approximately 30.41 GB of RAM per vCPU, specifically targeting enterprise architectures that require massive in-memory capacities.

Local storage includes 4398 GB of direct-attached solid-state drive (SSD) capacity, which functions alongside capability for Azure Premium Storage. The server operates without hardware GPU accelerators, directing all computational processing to its 128 dedicated execution threads. Complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included with the baseline instance provisioning.

The resource footprint of the M128dms_v2 reflects a specialized tier where memory density and local SSD scratch space are maximized relative to core count. From a qualitative cost perspective, dedicating massive RAM blocks and extensive local SSD storage to a single instance represents a high-density deployment model, minimizing the operational overhead of horizontally partitioning large stateful workloads. Due to its combination of 3.8+ TB of RAM and substantial local disk space, this server type is best suited for large in-memory databases such as SAP HANA, massive relational database management systems, heavy online analytical processing, and extensive enterprise transactional workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure M128dms_v2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor with an x86_64 Intel processing architecture. Designed for memory-intensive enterprise computing, the instance delivers 128 dedicated vCPUs and 3892.0 GB of system RAM, yielding a high ratio of 30.41 GB of memory per core. The server configuration bundles 4398 GB of local SSD temporary storage and supports Azure Premium Storage for persistent I/O workloads. GPU acceleration is absent, maintaining a focus on core compute and immense memory capacity. From an operational efficiency perspective, consolidating large memory footprints into a single host eliminates the partitioning overhead required by smaller instances. The M128dms_v2 is particularly suited for large-scale in-memory databases such as SAP HANA, enterprise relational databases, large in-memory caches, and heavy analytics or transaction processing environments.
